content.title: Marist guard wins Miss Georgia Basketball - The Champion Newspaper | 404-373-7779 | Georgia
content.text: Marist School guard Kate Harpring added another milestone to her high school basketball career on March 26, when she was named the 2026 Miss Georgia Basketball by the Atlanta Tip-Off Club. With the honor, Harpring becomes the first player in Marist’s program history to receive the award and just the third athlete from DeKalb County to earn the distinction, joining St. Pius’ Asia Durr (2014, 2015) and Southwest DeKalb’s Kayla Lewis (2010). The recognition is the latest in a long list of achievements for Harpring, who has firmly established herself as one of the most accomplished players in Georgia high school basketball history. Earlier this month, on March 12, she became the Georgia High School Association’s all-time leading scorer while leading Marist to a state championship victory over Kell High School—her second state title. Harpring’s dominance has extended beyond the state level. She was selected as a 2026 McDonald’s All-American, one of the most prestigious honors in high school basketball, awarded annually to just 24 players nationwide. In the showcase event, she will share the court with elite talent, including top-ranked recruits Saniya Hall and Jerzy Robinson. Her accolades also include being named the 2025 Atlanta High School Girls’ Metro Player of the Year and the Gatorade Girls’ Player of the Year for Georgia. Off the court, Harpring broke new ground by signing a Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) deal with Adidas, becoming one of only a handful of high school athletes to partner with the global brand. In her senior season, Harpring delivered career-best numbers, averaging 31 points, eight rebounds, and six assists per game. She led the Lady War Eagles to a fourth state championship in six years and closed out her high school career in fashion, scoring 40 points in the title game to earn player of the game honors. Looking ahead, Harpring will continue her basketball journey at the University of North Carolina, where she will play under head coach Courtney Banghart. With her scoring ability, leadership, and proven track record, she arrives in Chapel Hill as one of the most highly anticipated recruits in the country. 184 total views
